Re-running the migration drops any populated topic_embeds rows (losing the embed_url→topic mapping, which then causes TopicRetriever/EmbedController to re-import duplicate topics). Additionally, when a topic or post is deleted there is no cascade or cleanup hook, leaving orphaned topic_embeds rows whose topic_id_for_embed lookups return dead topic ids for EmbedController#best.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbedController#best enqueues a retrieve job and renders 'loading' for any embed_url on the embeddable host, with no validation that the URL is well-formed or reachable before enqueueing. This is a plausible abuse/DoS defect introduced by the diff; it is not contradicted by any code shown.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable compares URI(request.referer).host by exact string equality with SiteSetting.embeddable_host, with no normalization for case, port, or www prefix, and the setting has no place to express scheme or port. An embedding site served from www.eviltrout.com, from a non-default port, or with an uppercase host configured fails the referer check and 404s its embeds; conversely the same loose equality is the only access control for the endpoint, so the drift between how operators type the setting and how browsers emit referers decides who can embed — a configuration minefield rather than a real invariant.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: ensure_embeddable does `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, a raw exact string comparison against a setting defined as a plain string (embeddable_host: ''). No normalization for port, scheme, or www prefix exists anywhere in the diff, so a site served from a non-default port or www-prefixed host would fail the referer check and its embeds 404. Ruby's URI does downcase hosts, so the case claim is weak, but the port/www mismatch failure mode is real and grounded in the new code. This is a genuine correctness/operational defect

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed has no error handling around open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) or SimpleRSS.parse, and the job sets retry: false. A transient feed outage (timeout, DNS failure, malformed XML) raises, the run is not retried, and the failure is invisible except in logs — an operator with feed_polling_enabled gets no signal that imports stopped, and topics silently diverge from the feed for up to an hour (or indefinitely if the feed stays broken).

A transient error raises, is never retried, and there is no alerting/observability path added, so the operator gets no signal the hourly import stopped. This is a substantive operational/resilience risk created by this change (silent divergence from the feed), but not an incorrect-result defect in normal operation, so it fits important_non_bug.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed iterates the entire feed with no item cap or last-modified cutoff, and TopicEmbed.import does a fresh SELECT + SHA1 per item every hour regardless of change. A large feed causes an hourly O(N) full pass with one query per item and one PostRevisor pass per changed item on whatever single process runs the scheduled job; nothing in the design bounds the work, so feed size directly scales background cost with no pagination or batching escape hatch.

This is a real scalability/architecture concern created by the new code (hourly O(N) full-feed pass with per-item queries), not a correctness bug, and not generic advice since it cites specific code and a material consequence.

Operators who re-run a previously working Disqus import get a different artifact than before: network-dependent imports (can hang/fail per URL), raw-HTML posts bypassing the cooking pipeline, and topics created via the embed path — a changed output contract never surfaced as a decision point.

The observation is factually accurate and a maintainer-relevant behavior change to the disqus import tool (network dependence, different artifact). It is not a verifiable defect — the change appears deliberate within this PR — so it is a substantive non-bug review concern rather than a bug.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal state or error signal when retrieval never produces a topic. When fetch_http bails silently (embed_by_username blank, readability returns nothing, the remote URL 404s), TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed stays nil on every reload and the embedding page shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely, with the client polling the server forever — the async chain has no failure representation at the consumer boundary.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: loading.html.erb reloads via setTimeout(30000) whenever no topic exists; embed_controller's `best` enqueues RetrieveTopic whenever topic_id_for_embed returns nil; topic_retriever's fetch_http silently returns when embed_by_username is blank, and import returns nil on malformed URLs or failed retrieval. Thus a permanently failing retrieval yields an infinite reload loop with only 'Loading Discussion...' and no error state — a real behavioral defect (no failure path) introduced by this new feature.

records.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote calls `open(url).read` with no redirect, IP, or scheme constraint; the host allowlist is checked earlier in TopicRetriever against the original URL only, but open() silently follows redirects and re-resolves DNS. A page on embeddable_host (or any attacker page whose referer matches embeddable_host) can trigger a server-side fetch that 302-redirects (or DNS-rebinds after the host check) to 169.254.169.254, localhost, or internal services; the response body is parsed by Readability and portions (title/content) end up rendered in the embed page, leaking internal network data via SSRF. Note the /^https?\/\// gate in import runs only after the fetch has already happened.

records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, TopicEmbed.import writes content_sha1 via embed.update_column unconditionally after revisor.revise!, without checking whether the revision succeeded, so the stored sha1 can come to match content that was never actually persisted to the post. If revise! fails (validation, exception in the cooking pipeline, etc.), content_sha1 now equals the digest of the new remote contents while the post still holds the old raw text; the next poll computes the same sha1, skips the revision, and the source article's change is permanently lost — external edits are silently swallowed with no error anywhere.

When fetch_http bails (embed_by_username unset or user not found), TopicRetriever's host check rejects the URL, the throttle blocks the retry, or import fails, the embedded iframe shows 'Loading Discussion...' and re-requests /embed/best (enqueuing a retrieve job each time) forever on the publisher's page — an infinite reload loop with no error surfaced to the embedding site.
records.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: loading.html.erb unconditionally reloads every 30s; embed_controller#best enqueues RetrieveTopic whenever topic_id is nil; and TopicRetriever.retrieve silently no-ops when invalid_host?, retrieved_recently?, or fetch_http finds no user — so on permanent failure (e.g. bad host, missing embed_by_username user) the iframe reloads forever, re-requesting /embed/best indefinitely with no terminal error state. The mechanism is correctly described and grounded in the diff, though it's arguably a design gap rather than a crash.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration defaults posts.cook_method to 1, but Post.cook_methods assigns :regular=0 and :raw_html=1, so the migration labels every pre-existing post as raw_html. After migrating, every existing post's cook() returns raw markdown instead of cooked HTML (Post#cook short-circuits on cook_method == raw_html), silently breaking rendering of the entire post corpus; the default should be 0 (:regular).
records.rationale: Post.cook_methods Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns :regular=0, :raw_html=1. The migration adds cook_method with default: 1, and Post#cook returns raw when cook_method == raw_html, so all existing posts would render raw markdown. Verifiable directly from the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment test, not an origin equality test, so any origin that appears anywhere inside discourseUrl passes. A hostile embedding page whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl (trivially, any page when discourseUrl is short or when e.origin is a prefix like 'https://for') can post forged {type:'discourse-resize'} messages that control the iframe's rendered height — the boundary check the code exists to enforce does not actually bind the message to the Discourse origin.
records.rationale: The diff line `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js confirms the origin check is substring containment, not origin equality. Any e.origin that appears anywhere in discourseUrl (e.g., a prefix like 'https://for') passes, so the resize-message validation does not bind messages to the Discourse origin. The described mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff and constitutes a real defect in the intended security check.

records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed/HTML content as a post with cook_method :raw_html and Post#cook returns raw unfiltered, with no sanitize step anywhere in the import path. Arbitrary HTML/JavaScript from a remote RSS feed or imported article is stored as the post body and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (and everywhere cooked posts render), letting the feed publisher inject script into pages served on the forum's origin — a stored XSS vector gated only by the admin choosing to enable feed polling.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: Post#cook returns `raw` unfiltered when cook_method is raw_html, TopicEmbed.import creates posts from remote feed/article content with that cook_method and skip_validations, and the view renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so imported third-party HTML (including scripts) is served unfiltered on the forum origin — a real stored XSS vector introduced by this change.

records.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import (app/models/topic_embed.rb) calls `post = creator.create; if post.present? TopicEmbed.create!(...)` — a nil result silently skips embed creation with no logging or error, and the method then returns nil. PollFeed and EmbedController#best both treat this as 'not yet imported' with no signal of failure, so a permanently failing import (e.g., user/title invalid) leaves the embed page reloading indefinitely. This is a real, specific error-handling/observability gap in newly added logic rather than a verifiable broken behavior, so important_non_bug.
